Nvidia stock crash weighs down on HK tech shares, Hang Seng drops below 24,000 points
sum: Tech majors were weighed down by news of Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia's chief executive last night, with Hong Kong shares opening down 136 points.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 0.57 percent to 23,871 points, while the tech gauge dropped 0.35 percent to 3,918 points.
Tech heavyweights Alibaba (9988) and Tencent (0700) dipped 0.5 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively. Meituan (3690) declined 1.2 percent, and Xiaomi (1810) slipped 0.8 percent.

Local chipmakers rallied, with Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor gaining 2.79 percent as the best-performing blue chip, and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (0981) rising 2.59 percent after announcing its interim results yesterday. The company's third-quarter revenue rose 6.1 percent year on year to US$3.19 billion (HK$24.88 billion), and it expects revenue to rise 4-6 percent in the fourth quarter.

Link Real Estate Investment (0823) contracted 1.7 percent after reassuring shareholders of a stable rental outlook in yesterday's interim results press conference, with its total distributable amount for the first half of the 2026/2027 financial year up 0.4 percent to HK$3.3 billion.

Oil prices rose sharply, with Brent futures settling up to US$3 per barrel as escalating Middle East conflict and attacks on energy infrastructure overshadowed rising crude output. CNOOC (0883) rose 0.8 percent, and PetroChina (0857) rose 0.6 percent.
Chinese commercial aerospace company Adaspace Technology (6935) opened down 1.8 percent in its IPO debut.

Hang Seng Opens Lower as Hong Kong Bears the Tech Selloff's Weight
sum: Hong Kong is absorbing the global tech selloff while Shanghai barely moves, a 0.48% gap that shows where the offshore China trade is taking the pain. Mainland-listed names are insulated, leaving the Hang Seng exposed.
Hong Kong is absorbing the global tech selloff that mainland China is not: the Hang Seng opened down 0.48% while the SSE Composite moved just 0.04%.
That gap shows selling pressure concentrating in the offshore, internationally accessible slice of the China trade.
Hong Kong-listed technology names carry a more globally connected investor base, so they take the hit first while mainland-listed shares stay insulated by capital controls.
Investors with Chinese equity exposure should keep an eye on that spread through the session.

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks' Selloff Persists as Hang Seng Falls 307 Points, Narrowly Defending 24,000; Tech Names Hit Hardest
sum: Гонконгские акции продолжили свой слабый рост 12-го числа, при этом активные продажи в сфере технологий и интернет-компаний тянули широкий рынок вниз на протяжении всей сессии. Индекс Hang Seng закрылся на отметке 24 008,55, снизившись на 307,37 пункта, или 1,26%, зафиксировав четвертый дневной убыток подряд и едва удерживая уровень 24 000. Индекс Hang Seng Tech закрылся на отметке 3931,93, снизившись на 95,13 пункта, или на 2,36%, заметно отстав от основного рынка.

Глядя на структуру рынка, акции интернет-компаний с большой капитализацией упали практически по всем направлениям. Акции Alibaba (09988.HK) были среди голубых фишек с наихудшими показателями: в какой-то момент во время полуденной сессии они упали почти на 5%, а затем закрылись на уровне 95,6 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 12 долларов). Акции Kuaishou (01024.HK) также оказались под давлением, закрывшись на отметке 27,78 гонконгских долларов (около 3,5 долларов США), снизившись на 3,1%. JD.com (09618.HK) закрылся на уровне 107,2 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 14 долларов), снизившись на 3,5%; Tencent (00700.HK) закрылся на уровне 403,6 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 51 доллар), снизившись на 1,5%; и Meituan (03690.HK) закрылись на уровне 71,9 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 9,2 доллара), снизившись на 1,3%. Акции Xiaomi (01810.HK) держались относительно хорошо, поднявшись против тренда в полдень, а затем отступив вместе с более широким рынком в конце сессии.

Примечательно, что названия искусственного интеллекта и прикладного программного обеспечения различались. Запасы концептов больших моделей в целом упали: Zhipu резко упал, MINIMAX также снизился. Акции полупроводникового сектора, напротив, продемонстрировали устойчивость: Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) и Tianshu Zhixin (09911.HK) выросли, при этом Tianshu Zhixin выросла на 11% в полдень, а Biren Technology (06082.HK) также выросла почти на 7%. Акции SMIC (00981.HK) упали на 0,53%, указывая на то, что инвесторы придерживаются разных взглядов на полупроводники и крупные модели.

Металлы и активы-убежища одновременно ослабли, при этом акции золота и меди оказались под явным давлением. Котировки Zijin Gold International, Laopu Gold, China Nonferrous Mining (01258.HK) и China Molybdenum (03993.HK) снизились. China Molybdenum закрылась на уровне 12,18 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 1,6 доллара), снизившись на 3,7%, а Zijin Mining (02899.HK) закрылась на уровне 27,86 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 3,6 доллара), снизившись на 3,7%. Акции CK Hutchison (00001.HK) упали на 4,2% до 69,05 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 8,8 долларов), одной из самых слабых акций тяжеловесов на тот момент.

sum: Nvidia fell 3.7 percent in US after-hours trading after chief executive Jensen Huang admitted in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, while Hong Kong stocks opened higher on Monday on broad gains in technology shares.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index rose 143 points, or 0.59 percent, to 23,625 at the open, and the Hang Seng Tech Index advanced 1.02 percent to 4,119.

Major tech stocks mostly gained. Alibaba (9988) and Tencent (0700) rose 2.2 percent and 1.3 percent respectively, while Meituan (3690) advanced 0.3 percent. Among blue chips, Wuxi Biologics (2269) led the gains with a 2.9 percent rise.

Xiaomi (1810) opened 2 percent higher after reports that its electric vehicle unit had established a new international business department, covering international markets, go-to-market strategy, sales, network development, delivery and logistics, user services, general management and overseas regions.

Local chipmakers also advanced, supported by a 4.21 percent gain in the US Philadelphia Semiconductor Index on Friday. Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (0981) rose 2.2 percent, while Hua Hong Semiconductor (1347) climbed 2.6 percent.
Nvidia’s board is also set to launch an independent investigation into claims that Huang had been targeted by Chinese spies.

Alibaba's AI Push Hinges on Turning Compute Scarcity Into Paying Demand
sum: Alibaba's stock closed Friday with a 2.0% gain, a move that landed alongside a broader rebound in AI-linked equities following a two-day selloff. The advance came as the company's leadership used a high-profile platform to make the case for open-source artificial intelligence — while conceding that the hardware to run it is in short supply.

Chairman Joe Tsai, speaking Tuesday at the World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, touted the merits of open AI models and flagged bottlenecks in computing capacity as demand climbs, according to media reports. His remarks sketch both the promise and the pressure point for investors weighing whether Alibaba's AI buildout can pay for itself.

The Friday uptick was part of a wider recovery in technology names. AP reported a bounce after the two-day rout but drew no explicit link to Alibaba's own share movement. A day earlier, the stock had already ridden a broad rally in Hong Kong tech stocks: Reuters reported the Hang Seng Tech Index climbed 5%, with the agency pointing to improved market sentiment after the US midterm elections and tech names leading the gains.

Earlier in the week, media coverage tied rising Chinese equities to reports of planned central bank discussions on stronger credit support for share buybacks and stake increases. Alibaba was named among the beneficiaries; no additional financing was reported as having been agreed. Coverage also cited the planned integration of Alibaba's Qwen model into Apple's offering for the Chinese market — a December consumer launch of Apple Intelligence using the Alibaba model that was reported roughly a week ago.

The strategic logic Tsai outlined rests on a simple linkage: open models only generate value if there is enough infrastructure to serve them. That connection between technology and compute capacity is where Alibaba's approach will ultimately be judged.

The central question for investors is whether the company can convert growing AI usage into economically viable business. Supporting the bullish reading, Alibaba has already announced concrete deployments of its technology. The most telling evidence going forward would be signs that those deployments generate additional demand for Alibaba's cloud and AI services — and that the demand translates into revenue.

sum: HONG KONG: China and Hong Kong stocks fell on Friday as a Nasdaq-led tech rout rippled across Asia and fuelled fears the AI boom is losing steam, although bargain hunting helped pare losses in mainland markets buoyed by Beijing’s market-supporting measures.
China’s blue-chip CSI 300 Index dropped 1.4 percent, but notched up a 1.7 percent gain for the week to snap a 12-week-long losing streak.
The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.1 percent on Friday, though it ended the week 1.4 percent higher, breaking a six-week run of declines.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index was down 1.3 percent but registered a 5.1 percent weekly gain, its best since March 2025. The Hang Seng Tech Index slid 1.8 percent on Friday, but posted its best weekly gain since February 2025, advancing 8.6 percent.

Tech sectors across Asia took a heavy blow after a steep selloff overnight in the US wiped trillions of dollars off market value, as investors fretted that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could bring tighter scrutiny of the AI sector.
China’s tech-focused Star 50 Index and the AI Index slumped as much as 5.2 percent before paring some losses.
Dong Baozhen, chairman of asset manager Lingtong Shengtai, said the overnight slump in US tech stocks meant the logic behind the AI-driven rally had crumbled.

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks Surge on Heavy Volume: Hang Seng Index Rises 3.67%, Tencent, Alibaba and Other Tech Names Jump Over 7%
sum: On November 5, Hong Kong stocks pushed higher on heavy volume, with the Hang Seng Index closing up 3.67% and the Hang Seng Tech Index surging 5.55%, its biggest single-day gain since late February 2025.

Large-cap tech names strengthened across the board and served as the main engine driving the broader market. NetEase rose more than 9%, Alibaba and Xiaomi gained over 8%, Tencent Holdings climbed more than 7%, and JD.com and Meituan rose nearly 7%. Gold shares also advanced broadly, with Laopu Gold up more than 8% and Zhaojin Mining up over 5%. Consumer, auto, property and biopharma sectors posted the largest gains, while oil and petrochemicals, coal and semiconductors declined.
Fund flows were mixed. Southbound Funds recorded net selling of more than HK$21.3 billion (approximately $2.7 billion) on the day, in contrast to the sharp index rally.

Optical communications, memory and PCB concept stocks lagged, with Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable down more than 12% and Kingboard Laminates down more than 12%. Zhongji Innolight, CIG and Montage Technology each fell more than 6%, while GigaDevice dropped over 5%.

sum: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.42% to 23,393.32 on Monday 2 November 2026, its second straight gain, as the Hang Seng Tech Index surged 2.25% led by Xiaomi, CATL, Alibaba and Tencent, while banks and gold miners lagged.

The Hang Seng Index, the main benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, closed at 23,393.32 on Monday, up 98.90 points or 0.42%, according to Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing data reported by Xinhua and The Standard. It followed Friday's 1.5% rebound and marked the index's first session of November in positive territory.

The index traded as high as 23,543.30 but gave back part of those gains in the afternoon. The more significant move came in technology: the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 2.25% to 3,839.41 after rising as much as 3% intraday, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index added 0.56% to 7,906.11. Full-day turnover reached HK$204.84 billion.

Two forces supported the market. First, expectations of fresh policy support in mainland China lifted sentiment, after regulators met banks and brokers to discuss stabilising the equity market and the People's Bank of China signalled a new liquidity operation. Chinese brokerage stocks were among the leaders as investors bet on higher trading volumes.

Second, easing oil prices and a recovery in US stock futures after Friday's technology sell-off gave investors confidence to buy back into beaten-down tech names ahead of Apple's quarterly results. Even so, the gain in the broader Hang Seng was modest because banks and gold-related stocks, which had served as havens in October, were sold to fund purchases elsewhere.

Xiaomi was the best-performing blue chip, rising 6.1%, followed closely by battery giant CATL, which gained about 6% as lithium battery shares rallied. Among the heavyweights, Alibaba climbed 2.5% and Tencent advanced 2.2%, together providing a large share of the index's points gain.

Chipmakers also recovered. Hua Hong Semiconductor rose nearly 3% and SMIC added 1.5%. Casino operators climbed despite a decline in Macao's October gaming revenue, with Galaxy Entertainment up 3.7% and Sands China up 3.1%. On the downside, Bank of China and BOC Hong Kong were among the weakest constituents after their recent results, and gold miners eased.

sum: Weekly Review: Examining the "rewarded mistake" through the lens of southbound funds in Hong Kong stocks.

Close on Oct 30,$Hang Seng Index (800000.HK)$ at 23,294.42 points, up 0.87% for the week, ending two consecutive weeks of declines; $Hang Seng TECH Index (800700.HK)$ at 3,754.90 points, down 3.02% for the week; the SOE Index rose 1.37% for the week.

But what is truly glaring is not the indices, but the capital flows: Southbound funds recorded net sales of HKD 3.56 billion on Oct 30. This marks the 13th consecutive trading day of net selling, setting a new record for the longest streak of continuous net outflows, with cumulative outflows totaling HKD 37.323 billion over the 13-day period.Net outflows for the entire month of October approached HKD 28 billion, the largest single-month figure since July 2021.
Money is flowing out on one side, while indices are rising on the other.

The structural divergence is also stark: On Oct 30, consumer and energy sectors led the gains— $MAO GEPING (01318.HK)$ up over 13%, $MENGNIU DAIRY (02319.HK)$ up over 9%, $SINOPEC CORP (00386.HK)$ up 6.22%, $PETROCHINA (00857.HK)$ up 5.66%; meanwhile, the semiconductor sector continues to face pressure,$SMIC (00981.HK)$ down over 4%, $GIGADEVICE (03986.HK)$ down more than 8%. Looking at the full week,$SMIC (00981.HK)$ Down 8.67%, with southbound capital withdrawing approximately RMB 4.1 billion from it over the past seven days.
[But what is most worth pondering is this month's "rebound"]
